status.numerical_agreement_basis: Assessed on all 32 in-scope Table II targets (eight systems x accuracy, macro-precision, macro-recall, macro-F1), every one of which produced a comparable value. Absolute differences from the published two-decimal values range from 0.0303 to 7.8154 percentage points; only EfficientNet-B3 test accuracy (-0.0303) falls within the half-unit rounding interval of the paper's printed precision. Because the contract requires does_not_agree when any assessed value disagrees, the record is does_not_agree; no score-matching tolerance is asserted and no statistical significance test was performed. Recorded as a raw observation for later analysis, not as a scientific conclusion: the system ordering is not preserved and the paper's central claim inverts. The paper ties DenseNet121-HHO for best at 99.79% accuracy, while reproduced it is 95.1064% and seventh of eight; HHO lowered accuracy in both pairs (CNN 97.1878% to CNN-HHO 91.0546%; DenseNet121 96.3922% to DenseNet121-HHO 95.1064%) where the paper reports it helping or holding level. The best reproduced system is EfficientNet-B0 at 99.3895%.

datasets.name: ArASL2018 / Arabic Alphabets Sign Language Dataset
datasets.version_or_subset: Hugging Face snapshot pain/ArASL_Database_Grayscale (single 'train' split; parquet), revision 114709884276379a01e0722d71cd590c8ad3a05d
datasets.license_or_permission: CC BY 4.0 (Hugging Face dataset card); underlying corpus is Latif, Mohammad, Alghazo, AlKhalaf & AlKhalaf, "ArASL: Arabic Alphabets Sign Language Dataset," Data in Brief 23:103777, 2019, released 'publicly available and free for all researchers.' Permits this project-cloud training run.
datasets.notes: The single 54,049-image/32-class 'train' split is repartitioned into the paper's own 64/16/20 stratified train/validation/test split at run time (Algorithm 1); there is no author-published test split to match. Identity check: exact 54,049 total and exact 32-class label set independently match both the paper's stated dataset size and the Data in Brief description; native per-image resolution is 64x64 grayscale for 53,401/54,049 rows, with 648 rows (1.2%) natively 256x256 or 768x1024 (10 of those RGB) -- consistent with the original corpus's reported per-image dimension variation, and handled by the paper's own resize-to-64x64 preprocessing step rather than being a data-integrity problem. The paper cites two Mendeley listings for what states the same 54,049-image/32-class corpus (refs [18] DOI 10.17632/6y5dwtrdth.1 and [19] Data in Brief 10.1016/j.dib.2019.103777); this Hugging Face mirror's homepage points to the [19] listing (data.mendeley.com/datasets/y7pckrw6z2/1). The Mendeley original was not independently re-downloaded because the mirror's exact sample/class counts and per-image characteristics already establish dataset identity.

guesses_and_deviations.description: Whether augmentation includes a horizontal flip.
guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Algorithm 1's augmentation list is rotation, zoom, shift, and brightness, with no flip; Fig. 8's "Image processing" box lists Rescaling, Zooming, Shifting, Brightness Adjustment, and Horizontal Flip
guesses_and_deviations.basis: Algorithm 1 is the one place the paper actually spells out the augmentation procedure

guesses_and_deviations.description: How much of each pretrained backbone is frozen.
guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: DenseNet121 (§III.B.5): "the early layers of the network were frozen... focusing the training process on the remaining layers for fine-tuning"; ResNet50 (§III.B.3): "with the early layers frozen to preserve pre-learned features". EfficientNet-B0/B3 are only "fine-tuned" (§III.B.2), and DenseNet201's description (§III.B.4) does not mention freezing. No layer count for "early"
guesses_and_deviations.used: Partial unfreezing: ResNet50 last 10 of 174 layers; EfficientNet-B3 last 35 of 381; DenseNet201 last 125 of 704; DenseNet121 (both variants) last 200 of 424; EfficientNet-B0 all 234
guesses_and_deviations.basis: The smallest trailing-layer count whose trainable-parameter count gets close to the from-scratch CNN's ~4.5M; a stopping rule based on parameter count, not on any accuracy number. "Match the CNN's parameter count" is this attempt's own rule, not something the paper states
guesses_and_deviations.effect: The whole-backbone reading was built first. It trained only 262K-543K parameters per pretrained model and the CNN beat every pretrained model. Partial unfreezing closed most of the gap (DenseNet201 from 28 points behind to 2, DenseNet121 from 14 to 3.4, ResNet50 from 18 to 3.8)
guesses_and_deviations.scope: EfficientNet-B0, EfficientNet-B3, ResNet50, DenseNet201, DenseNet121, DenseNet121-HHO

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Algorithm 1 says the augmented generator covers training and validation; only the test generator skips augmentation
guesses_and_deviations.used: Training and validation augmented; test gets plain normalization
guesses_and_deviations.effect: The fitness signal the two HHO searches optimize against is computed on augmented validation data

guesses_and_deviations.description: How grayscale images become the RGB input the paper describes.
guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: "All images were resized to 64 × 64 pixels and retained in RGB format" (§III.A); Figs. 2, 6, and 7 show 64x64x3 input
guesses_and_deviations.used: Every image converted to grayscale and resized to 64x64 (648 of 54,049 are not native 64x64 grayscale), then the single channel replicated into 3 channels
guesses_and_deviations.basis: The native ArASL2018 images are 64x64 grayscale

guesses_and_deviations.description: Input scaling for the pretrained backbones.
guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Algorithm 1 normalizes images to [0, 1] ahead of every model
guesses_and_deviations.used: The [0, 1] scaling is undone and each backbone's own `preprocess_input` applied (mean-subtracted BGR for ResNet50, x/127.5-1 for DenseNet, EfficientNet's internal Rescaling+Normalization)
guesses_and_deviations.basis: Each tf.keras.applications backbone was pretrained with its own preprocessing on raw [0, 255] input
guesses_and_deviations.effect: Without it, ResNet50 reached ~34% test accuracy after 60 epochs and EfficientNet never escaped chance accuracy
guesses_and_deviations.scope: EfficientNet-B0, EfficientNet-B3, ResNet50, DenseNet201, DenseNet121, DenseNet121-HHO

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Fig. 4: EfficientNet-B0/B3 take a 224x224x3 input; the shared preprocessing produces 64x64x3
guesses_and_deviations.used: Upsize with a Keras Resizing layer to 224x224

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Fig. 2: Conv2D(32), Conv2D(32), Conv2D(64), Conv2D(128), with feature maps 64x64x32, 32x32x32, 16x16x64, 14x14x128, 7x7x128 and a Flatten of 6272 before Dense(512)
guesses_and_deviations.used: Three blocks of two same-padded 3x3 convolutions (32, 64, 128 filters), each followed by MaxPooling and BatchNormalization; Flatten of 8192 before Dense(512)
guesses_and_deviations.effect: About 4.5M trainable parameters, against about 3.3M for Fig. 2's shapes (the Flatten-to-Dense(512) layer alone is 4.2M vs 3.2M). The CNN's ~4.5M is the target of the backbone-freezing rule

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: The last layer uses sigmoid for 32-way classification
guesses_and_deviations.basis: Sigmoid doesn't make sense for a single-label, mutually-exclusive classification problem, and every other model in the paper uses softmax for the same task; the sigmoid mention is treated as a slip in the writing

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Fig. 6: MaxPooling2D, BatchNormalization, Dropout (0.3), Flatten, Dense (512 units, ReLU), Dropout (0.5), Dense (32 units, Sigmoid)
guesses_and_deviations.used: MaxPooling2D, BatchNormalization, Flatten, Dense (512, ReLU), Dropout, Dense (32, softmax): no Dropout (0.3) before Flatten. The remaining dropout is 0.5 for DenseNet121 and HHO-tuned for DenseNet121-HHO

guesses_and_deviations.description: Learning rate for the models whose rate the paper omits.
guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: The paper names an optimizer (Adam or Adamax) for each but never gives a rate
guesses_and_deviations.used: The framework default for ResNet50, DenseNet121, and DenseNet201; 1e-4 for the plain CNN
guesses_and_deviations.basis: For the CNN, Adam's default (1e-3) was tried first and collapsed to predicting the class prior; 1e-4 is the value CNN-HHO's own search converged to
evidence: train.py make_model_specs() comment on the CNN spec

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: Figure 5 just says "Flatten → Dropout → Dense" with no number
guesses_and_deviations.basis: A plain default, distinct from the two dropout rates the paper does give for other models (0.6 for EfficientNet, 0.8 for DenseNet201)

guesses_and_deviations.description: How precision, recall, and F1 are averaged across the 32 classes.
guesses_and_deviations.basis: The standard choice when it isn't specified, and consistent with the paper's own numbers: its F1 is sometimes lower than both its precision and recall, which can't happen with micro-averaging but is normal under macro or per-class averaging on an imbalanced label set

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: 64/16/20, stratified; the split itself and a seed are not published
"Table II presents the best test results for each model" (§IV); it does not say best over what (epochs, runs, or HHO candidates)
guesses_and_deviations.used: One test evaluation at the end of the epoch count Table II lists; no checkpoint or run selection

guesses_and_deviations.description: Accuracies quoted in the results prose.
guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: §IV's prose gives EfficientNet-B3 98.55%, ResNet50 97.90%, and CNN 94.50% with F1 94.2%; none of these appear in Table II
guesses_and_deviations.used: Table II's values as the targets

guesses_and_deviations.paper_says: HHO tunes "the learning rate, batch size, number of filters, and dropout rates" for CNN-HHO (§III.B.6, Fig. 7) and "learning rate, batch size, and dropout, to maximize validation accuracy" for DenseNet121-HHO (§III.B.7); no search ranges, population size, number of iterations, or cost per candidate evaluation
guesses_and_deviations.used: Search ranges: log10 learning rate [-4, -2], batch size 16-64, dropout 0.2-0.6, and for CNN-HHO a filter-count scale 0.5-1.5. Population 6, 4 iterations; each candidate judged by training it for 3 epochs on a 25% slice of the training data
guesses_and_deviations.basis: Evaluating every candidate with a full training run would cost far more than the 5-epoch final run the paper reports; a fairly standard cheap-proxy setup
guesses_and_deviations.effect: DenseNet121-HHO's search settled on a configuration that does slightly worse than the plain DenseNet121 default (95.11% vs. 96.39%), reported as-is rather than re-running the search until it beats the baseline
